nodes.title: Newton's laws of motion
nodes.subtitle: force, mass and acceleration
summary: A force changes how an object moves: F = ma.
Every action has an equal and opposite reaction.
details: Published: Isaac Newton set out the three laws in the Principia (1687).
Still used: They describe everyday motion very well; relativity and quantum physics take over at very high speeds and very small scales.

nodes.title: Noether's theorem
nodes.subtitle: symmetry gives conservation laws
summary: Every continuous symmetry of the laws of physics gives a conserved quantity.
Same laws at every time → energy is conserved; at every place → momentum.
details: Proved: Emmy Noether proved it in 1918 (English translation 1971).
Everywhere: Rotation symmetry gives conservation of angular momentum; the symmetries of the Standard Model give conserved charges.
